newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel mulls raising bank ownership limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel mulls raising bank ownership limit.

text.p: A presidential commission examining financial reform in South Korea plans to recommend increasing the individual shareholding limit in banks, a panel statement said on Wednesday.

The Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said it was working on a plan to raise the ceiling to 10 percent from the current four percent. The limit would be applied to city, regional and joint venture banks.
The statement said the panel was considering increasing the limit to establish reponsible management in banks and to improve their competitiveness.
The 31-member commission was set up in January after President Kim Young-sam said he would push forward with reforming the financial sector.
The commission also agreed in principle to introduce financial holding companies. But such companies would not be allowed in non-financial industries such as manufacturing and distribution.
Financial holding companies would be required to submit consolidated financial statements and to set up a firewall betweeb itself and its affiliates.
A formal proposal is expected be presented by the end of May.
